subject: Shiproom briefing: trajectory, sprint ownership, and release contingencies
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reid <tom.reid@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Shiproom briefing: trajectory, sprint ownership, and release contingencies

Team — attaching a compact snapshot for the QBR shiproom tomorrow. High-level summary:

- Current trajectory: core inference runtime SLOs are green for the hosted tier, but a late integration from the customer's observability agent is creating an intermittent increase in tail latency for some 2k-seq tests. Details in attachment (integration-lag_matrix.xlsx).
- Launch timeline: customer pilot scheduled for 2027-04-21. We have three remaining engineering milestones: final quantization tuning, integration QA, and canary policy validation.
- Risks: the observability plugin (3rd-party) requires a custom buffer change that may require a hotfix in the runtime image. If we miss the QA window (next two sprints), pilot may be delayed.

Asks:
1) Monica — please confirm owner for the runtime hotfix and an estimate for a 2-week hotfix + validation path.
2) Aditya — sync with the product PM on canary validation criteria we promised Acme; I put the doc link in Drive.
3) Vivek — we may need an exec-level exception to expand dedicated capacity for the pilot if latency stays noisy; flagging now so procurement can be prepared.

Attachments: QBR_shiproom_snapshot_v1.pdf, integration-lag_matrix.xlsx

Thanks — I'll be in the shiproom at 9:45 for a quick walkthrough.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reid <tom.reid@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Shiproom briefing: trajectory, sprint ownership, and release contingencies

Naomi — thanks for the snapshot and matrix. Quick responses below.

- Hotfix owner: assigning to Rahul (eng lead on runtime) and I've created a short ticket in our sprint board. Rahul estimates 8 dev days + 2 QA days if it's a single-image change; 12+ dev days if kernel-level tweaks are required (depending on the plugin's buffering). I asked him to drop more detail by EOD.
- Canary criteria: Aditya, can you confirm the two acceptance gates we promised Acme (p99 tail <= 350ms on 2k-seq; no degradation in throughput >5% for baseline traffic)? We should publish a checklist.
- Contingency: I'm adding a fallback play — if hotfix slips, we run the pilot in a reduced-seq mode (max 512) and enable aggressive KV-prefix caching to keep tail latency acceptable. That still requires a customer-facing note.

I'll join the shiproom walkthrough at 9:45.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Manager, Engineering Programs | Redwood Inference

On 3 Apr 2027, at 09:12, Naomi Feldman wrote:
> Team — attaching a compact snapshot for the QBR shiproom tomorrow....
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T12:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Shiproom briefing: trajectory, sprint ownership, and release contingencies

Appreciate the heads-up, Naomi. A couple of leadership asks: 

1) Please prepare a two-slide exec summary for the QBR highlighting (a) customer impact vector, (b) showstopper risk if the hotfix goes >2 weeks, and (c) recommended next-step (allow reserve dedicated capacity for pilot). I'll present this if you can get it to me before 5pm PST.

2) If Rahul confirms kernel work is required, escalate immediately — I'll approve a small contractor budget to compress schedule.

3) Monica — the reduced-seq pilot option is acceptable as a fallback, but ensure we have a comms note drafted for Tom (Acme) so expectations are explicit. I'd like a one-page MOP (method of procedure) for the fallback path.

One more: make sure the QBR snapshot calls out which SLAs we'd be stretching — token-level cost and p99 latency specifically. That helps legal/procurement model the ask.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product | Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-04-03T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Shiproom briefing: trajectory, sprint ownership, and release contingencies — action plan

Filing a short update after our shiproom:

Decisions & owners: 
- Hotfix: Rahul (Eng) — scope limited to runtime image buffer change; estimate 10 business days including QA. Ticket: ENG-6742.
- Canary validation gates: Aditya to publish checklist by 2027-04-05.
- Fallback MOP: Monica to deliver one-page fallback comms + MOP by 2027-04-06.
- Exec ask: Vivek will request a reserved-capacity exception for the pilot if we see >15% p99 variance in the next two smoke runs.

Customer comms: Tom — we'll share the fallback MOP before the pilot and confirm the reduced-seq pilot option if needed. No change to the 2027-04-21 pilot date yet; we're treating this as high-priority to keep that target.

Links: shiproom folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqQBR-shiproom; HubSpot: 1245789

Attachments included in thread: QBR_shiproom_snapshot_v1.pdf, integration-lag_matrix.xlsx

Thanks all — I'll track the action items and update the QBR pack.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
